claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but is brittle.
Stress concentration at the incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces causes the initial brittleness.
Treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will topologically transform the lamellar microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will produce a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
The HPHT treatment will transform incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces into coherent interfaces.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the phases.
The transformed microstructure promotes dislocation glide, stacking-fault formation, and twinning.
Dislocation transfer and the additional deformation mechanisms promote homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution arrests interfacial cracking.
The HPHT treatment will significantly improve ductility without substantially reducing strength.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated crack-propagation morphology on its fracture surface.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after HPHT treatment.
The untreated alloy exhibits isolated microcracks at incoherent interfaces.
The untreated alloy exhibits divergent GND densities between the FCC and B2 phases during deformation.
A pressure-temperature window exists that induces interface coherence while avoiding phase decomposition, instability, or melting.
HPHT treatment is known to enhance diffusion and interface coherence in other material systems.
The specific FCC/B2 topological transformation in Al0.7CoCrFeNi at exactly 6 GPa and 1473 K has not been definitively established.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts arrest of interfacial cracking, yet the proposed positive fracture-surface signature is elongated crack propagation, contrasted with isolated microcracks in the brittle baseline. As written, greater crack elongation is not clearly consistent with crack arrest and could instead indicate more extensive propagation.
